question.prompt:
Each of the following four large congruent squares is subdivided into combinations of congruent triangles or rectangles and is partially shaded. What percent of the total area is partially shaded?

[Figure 1](figures/2011_AMC_8_Q07_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Because the four large squares are congruent, use the area of one large square as the unit of area.

Using the given congruent subdivisions, the top-left square has one of four equal strips shaded, and the bottom-right square has one of four equal small squares shaded. Each contributes \(\frac14\) of a large square.

In the top-right square, the shaded triangle is half of one of the four equal small squares, so its area is \(\frac18\) of a large square. The bottom-left square has one whole small square and half of another shaded, giving \(\frac14+\frac18=\frac38\) of a large square.

The combined shaded area, in large-square units, is
\[
\frac14+\frac18+\frac38+\frac14
=\frac28+\frac18+\frac38+\frac28
=1.
\]
The total area is \(4\) large-square units, so the shaded percentage is
\[
\frac14=\frac{25}{100}=\boxed{25\%},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Measure in large-square units
